definition: When drawing a smear as wobbled/squiggled distortion lines plus speed lines, every line must run PARALLEL to the object's own direction of motion and to each other — the direction the squiggles are drawn in is itself what tells the viewer which way the object is moving, and even a slight inconsistency in that parallel direction breaks both the illusion of speed and the clarity of the action, independent of how intense or well-drawn the individual squiggles are.
purpose: Make a smear communicate a single, unambiguous direction of motion, since the squiggle/line direction IS the mechanism the viewer reads that direction from, not just a texture.
visible_effect: A smeared shape's surface is covered in short wobbled lines and speed lines that all run in the same direction, at varying size and spacing (deliberately irregular, not evenly spaced) — demonstrated directly on screen with a side-by-side comparison labeled 'CLEAR DIRECTION' (all squiggles parallel) against 'NOT CLEAR DIRECTION' (squiggles pointing inconsistently), on an otherwise identical circular smear shape.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: A viewer reads directional intent directly from line orientation; even a small deviation from parallel is stated to break the illusion of speed and the clarity of the action, not merely to look slightly worse — this is framed as a hard requirement, not a matter of degree.
physical_interpretation: An imitation of real motion blur's directional streaking, not a literal physical claim.
use_cases: any hand-drawn smear or distortion effect on a fast-moving object, where every added squiggle/speed-line must be checked against the object's own true direction of travel
increasing a smear's apparent speed by increasing squiggle-line intensity/density while keeping direction strictly consistent
non_use_cases: a slow or static object, where no directional squiggle vocabulary is needed at all

an object changing direction WITHIN the smeared span (e.g. a bounce or a sharp turn), where a single uniform squiggle direction would misrepresent the actual path — this case needs the smear broken into direction-consistent segments rather than one uniform pass
interactions: motion_smear_readability (W01) — the general existing card for the technique; this entry adds a specific, hard, visually-demonstrated failure condition (line-direction inconsistency) that card does not itself state
prep_smear_slowdown_three_phase_smear_structure (this same video) — this entry's rule applies specifically to the SMEAR phase of that broader three-phase structure

style_variations.anime: a standard, expected convention for hand-drawn action
style_variations.realistic: not applicable — smears are explicitly non-physical readability aids regardless of style

cadence_representation: Not representable: Cadence has no mesh deformation at all (the existing `motion_smear_readability` card's own stated limitation), so no drawn squiggle/line vocabulary is reachable in this build regardless of direction-consistency rules. If a future VFX-trail approximation were built (per `arc_trail_vfx_readability`, W01), this entry's rule would translate directly: any trail/streak geometry generated would need to align with the object's own instantaneous velocity direction, which `ai/motion.js sampleMotion`'s existing `linear_velocity` measurement already provides.
control_surface: None — no drawing/VFX tool in this build reaches this technique.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Not measurable in this build directly (no mesh deformation or drawn-line data exists), but the underlying velocity-direction data a future implementation would need to check against IS already measured: `ai/motion.js sampleMotion`'s `linear_velocity` gives the exact direction any generated smear/trail geometry would need to stay parallel to.
generation_or_modification_methods: None currently reaches this in this build.
failure_modes: squiggle/speed lines drawn at even slightly inconsistent angles, breaking both the speed illusion and the action's clarity — demonstrated directly, not merely described, in the source's own side-by-side comparison
evenly-spaced, evenly-sized squiggles — the source separately notes this looks unnatural and that deliberate randomness in size/spacing is also required alongside direction consistency
roblox_considerations: Would apply identically to any custom line/streak VFX built for Roblox (e.g. a shader-drawn or texture-based streak effect) — direction consistency against the object's own velocity would be exactly as load-bearing there.
examples: 'the direction you draw these squiggles indicates the direction that the object is moving... everything should be parallel — if your squiggles and lines are going in different directions, even just a little, the illusion of speed and clearness of the action won't get across' (video @ 00:50–01:22), directly illustrated on screen with a labeled 'CLEAR DIRECTION' vs 'NOT CLEAR DIRECTION' side-by-side comparison (frame at t=00:45)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/5v0IZSr9-j0 (Kuzillon) @ 00:50–01:22, confirmed directly in this session's frame at t=00:45 (a labeled 'CLEAR DIRECTION'/'NOT CLEAR DIRECTION' comparison image); experimental until validated
